01-parallel-coords-sparkline-table.visual_critic_note: Consistently applied indigo accent, clean card layout with good whitespace, and a thoughtful parallel-coords + sparkline-table pairing elevate this above generic, though Tableau10 for region colors and 150-line density keep it short of polished.
01-parallel-coords-sparkline-table.encoding_integrity_note: Zero baselines correct, data-driven extents on all parallel-coord axes, no size/area encoding issues, but sparkline histograms use a hardcoded threshold of 24 bins rather than a data-driven rule (Sturges'/Scott's), and fg-bar data joins lack key functions.
01-parallel-coords-sparkline-table.stress_test_note: Every pointermove during strumming synchronously calls updateSelection()→drawLines()+updateTable() with no RAF/dirty-flag throttling, and x/y scales are captured in static closures with no resize handler to refresh them.
01-parallel-coords-sparkline-table.cognitive_load_note: Two linked views, 6-color regional encoding (within perceptual limits), and opacity-layered canvas rendering manage 150 lines reasonably well, but the unfiltered default state shows a dense color tangle that requires interaction to resolve.

15-adjacency-matrix-reorder.visual_critic_note: Thoughtful hover interaction and meaningful gray/colored encoding for cross- vs intra-community edges lift it above generic, but schemeCategory10 palette and flat typographic hierarchy keep it from feeling deliberately designed.
15-adjacency-matrix-reorder.encoding_integrity_note: Bar chart uses data-driven zero-based domain (d3.max for maxDegree), opacity domain [0,10] is hardcoded but exactly matches the synthetic weight generation range (1–10), no radius deception or dual-axis fabrication, and reordering correctly updates scale domains rather than re-joining data.
15-adjacency-matrix-reorder.stress_test_note: updateOrder() starts a 1200ms staggered transition with no .interrupt() call, so rapid button clicks during animation cause mid-flight snapping; mouseover also bulk-updates all 1225 cells on every cell entry but lacks touch event filtering.
15-adjacency-matrix-reorder.cognitive_load_note: 35×35 matrix with 5-color community encoding and linked bar chart is clean and well-structured, but cell size (~16px) is near the minimum for comfortable reading and the staggered wave reorder animation — while aesthetic — makes it hard to track individual node positions during transition.

16-sankey-energy-flow.visual_critic_note: Dark background and source-to-target gradient links show genuine effort, but schemeCategory10 produces a noisy rainbow across nodes and the flat typographic hierarchy (all labels same size/weight) prevents it from feeling deliberately designed.
16-sankey-energy-flow.encoding_integrity_note: Sankey link widths and node heights are correctly proportional to flow values via d3-sankey layout; dynamicTotal is data-driven; no baseline, radius-deception, or dual-axis violations apply; minor deductions for synthetic data and absent key functions (acceptable since no data updates occur).
16-sankey-energy-flow.stress_test_note: Drag handler calls sankey.update(graph) and redraws all 37 link paths on every mousemove with no RAF or throttling; no touch event filtering or .filter() guard on the drag behavior leaves mobile scroll/drag unresolved.
16-sankey-energy-flow.cognitive_load_note: 22 nodes and 37 gradient-blended links create mid-chart density that's hard to trace statically, but the hover-to-fade interaction and clear 5-column layout manage it well enough that the viewer can orient without overload.

39-quadtree-hit-detection.visual_critic_note: Dark background with a vibrant radial color-coded point cloud looks polished and purposeful; the glowing hit-detection interaction and clean UI panel show genuine design intent, though the rainbow 8-category palette edges toward busy.
39-quadtree-hit-detection.encoding_integrity_note: No encoding violations apply — fixed-radius circles encode no quantitative data, color is categorical and correct, and the identity xScale/yScale are appropriate for a spatial coordinate visualization, though hardcoded viewport domains rather than data-driven extents limit robustness.
39-quadtree-hit-detection.stress_test_note: The zoom handler unconditionally calls buildQuadtree (O(n) over 5000 points), drawBackground, drawVoronoi (full Delaunay recompute when enabled), and drawInteraction on every scroll/pinch frame with no requestAnimationFrame coalescing or dirty-flag throttling; pointermove is canvas-only and lightweight, no stale-closure, infinite-loop, mid-flight, or touch-fight issues found.
39-quadtree-hit-detection.cognitive_load_note: Single-view with 8 categories hits the color warning threshold, but strong spatial separation of radial clusters and a dark high-contrast background make each color group immediately identifiable; the interaction layer (10-nearest lines on hover) is focused and adds no visual noise at rest.

53-textured-raincloud.visual_critic_note: Dual-encoding with Tol palette + distinct SVG patterns is a genuinely considered accessibility design choice, layout is clean with good whitespace, but the six-color categorical palette at 50% opacity creates a slightly muddy mid-tone feel and the absence of any legend forces reliance on y-axis labels alone.
53-textured-raincloud.encoding_integrity_note: KDE uses principled Silverman bandwidth (with documented bimodal adjustment), boxplot stats are correctly computed, and x-scale domain is data-driven via d3.max, but the x-axis lower bound is hardcoded to 0 rather than data-driven, leaving unnecessary empty space on the left for distributions ranging ~30–100.
53-textured-raincloud.stress_test_note: Visualization is almost entirely static with no brush, zoom, or drag interactions — the sole interaction is a checkbox CSS class toggle, so none of the five stress-test failure modes (update storm, infinite loop, stale scale, mid-flight snap, touch fight) are applicable.
53-textured-raincloud.cognitive_load_note: 6 groups, 6 colors (Tol bright palette), triple-layer encoding per row (violin + boxplot + jitter) requires brief orientation but is consistent and readable across all rows with no animation or multi-view complexity.

68-animated-sparkline-table.visual_critic_note: Cohesive dark theme with semantic color palette (blue/green/amber/red mapped consistently across KPI charts, table sparklines, and status badges), clear typographic hierarchy, and four distinct KPI chart types show genuine design intent — docked by the memory bullet chart feeling weaker than the other three KPI visualizations and the large dead space below the table.
68-animated-sparkline-table.encoding_integrity_note: Table sparkline areas use d3.extent (non-zero) domain so filled area doesn't represent magnitude from zero, and the memory KPI has hardcoded magic-number values (68, 85) rather than data-driven bindings; otherwise scales are data-driven, shared cross-row domains enable honest comparison, and the table uses correct key functions for object constancy.
flags: Update Storm (resize handler calls all 4 KPI redraws on every resize event without debounce/throttle)
Mid-Flight Snap (Replay button calls init() which removes DOM and starts new transitions without .interrupt() on in-flight animations)
68-animated-sparkline-table.stress_test_note: Unthrottled resize redraws all KPI charts at 60fps and the Replay button lacks .interrupt() guards, but no brush/zoom storms, no cross-view dispatch loops, no stale scale closures, and no touch/mouse fight since only a click button is used.
68-animated-sparkline-table.cognitive_load_note: Clean two-tier hierarchy (4 KPI cards + 6-row table) with consistent 3-color encoding across all 18 table sparklines; only mild friction is the KPI row using four different chart types (area, bar, win-loss, bullet) requiring per-card decoding rather than a unified encoding.

90-skill-growth-sparklines.visual_critic_note: Deliberate design with per-category color-coded badges, solid typographic hierarchy, and a smart shared y-domain (0–100) across sparklines for direct comparison — let down slightly by the sparklines being small enough that the faint area fill reads as decoration rather than data encoding.
90-skill-growth-sparklines.encoding_integrity_note: Shared [0,100] y-domain enables honest cross-row comparison, area y0 correctly anchors at zero (data value 0 maps to baseline), key function d=>d.name maintains object constancy on sort, but no line.defined() guard for missing values.
90-skill-growth-sparklines.stress_test_note: No brush, zoom, or drag interactions exist; only click-to-sort triggers renderTable(), which is infrequent and non-continuous, so none of the five interaction traps apply.
90-skill-growth-sparklines.cognitive_load_note: Clean tabular layout with shared y-axis sparklines, restrained single-hue encoding, and 7 badge colors used as labels not data marks — cognitive load is minimal and cross-row comparison is effortless.

96-regional-parcoords-grid.visual_critic_note: Tableau-derived palette and linked brushing across panels show real design intent, but solid-stroke colored lines without alpha lose density information, and the typography hierarchy is minimal — functional and readable but not crafted.
96-regional-parcoords-grid.encoding_integrity_note: Parallel coordinates with data-driven y-scales via d3.extent over the full dataset (shared across all panels for honest cross-region comparison), no area/baseline encoding violations, and correct brush synchronization; only minor issue is all lines batched into a single canvas path, preventing per-line opacity control.
96-regional-parcoords-grid.stress_test_note: brush handler calls updateCanvases() (4 full canvas redraws) on every mousemove with no RAF or debounce, and yScales are captured as static closures with no resize handler to refresh them.
96-regional-parcoords-grid.cognitive_load_note: 4-panel 2×2 small-multiples parallel coordinates with one color per region reads cleanly — the background-grey/foreground-color dimming pattern keeps individual panels legible, and the 4-color palette is well-separated, but dense line crossings within each panel (50 lines × 6 axes) approach spaghetti threshold and the cross-panel brush-sync interaction cannot be assessed from a static screenshot.
